glosses: To cover something with planking.

examples.text: to plank a floor or a ship
Plank'd with pine.

glosses: To bake (fish, etc.) on a piece of cedar lumber.

examples.text: Along the lower river, planked shad dinners (baked and broiled) were highly popular during the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries.

glosses: To lay down, as on a plank or table; to stake or pay cash.

examples.text: to plank money in a wager
Joe planked the money down in the officer of a newspaper editor and awaited results. There weren't any.

examples.text: The woman, known as Claudia, fell from a 2m wall after earlier demonstrating the wrong way to plank on a small stool while holding a bottle of wine. A friend said some guests had not heard of planking and Claudia was demonstrating how ridiculous it was.
Perth man Simon Carville became an internet sensation after he was photographed planking naked in the arms of famous Perth statue the Eliza.
